how-to-price-a-csa-share.html.text:
CSA Share Pricing Calculator · guide

How to price a CSA share: the math

Short answer: add up what a season of boxes costs you in inputs, packing, delivery and fees, add your hours at the wage you need, spread your fixed costs over the shares you will sell, and only then check the result against the retail value members receive. Pricing from the market first is how a full box ends up paying a few dollars an hour.

A worked example

A ten-week season. Each box holds two bags of salad at $5 retail, $0.80 cost and 5 minutes of labour each for all ten weeks, and three pounds of tomatoes at $4 retail, $0.60 cost and 4 minutes each for six weeks. Packaging is $1 a box, packing takes 5 minutes, the payment fee is 3%, fixed season costs are $1,000, and you sell 40 shares at $150.

  • Retail value per share: $172.00, so members get 1.15 times what they pay.
  • Item cost $26.80 plus box costs $10.00; each share takes 3.7 hours of your time.
  • Each share contributes $108.70 after fees and costs, so 40 shares earn $3,348.00 before your own pay: 148 hours, or $22.62 an hour.
  • Paying yourself $20 an hour leaves $388.00 of profit, and the price that pays exactly $20 an hour at 40 shares is $140.00.

Drop to 28 shares and the same price no longer covers the fixed costs and your hours; the break-even is 29 shares at $20 an hour. The CSA Share Pricing Calculator runs this on any box, with the price sweep.

How the answer is found

  1. Each item is summed over the weeks it is in the box: retail value, cost and minutes.
  2. Profit before your pay is shares times (price after fee, minus item cost, minus box costs) minus fixed costs; after your pay it also subtracts hours at your rate.
  3. The wage price and the break-even share count are closed-form; the price sweep re-runs the season with members falling as price rises by the elasticity you set.

Questions

How do I value my hours?

Use what you would pay someone to do the work, or what the farm needs to clear for you to stay in business. The calculator shows both your result at an hourly rate you choose and the price that pays a target wage.

Should the price follow the retail value of the box?

Retail value is a ceiling on what members will accept, not a floor on what you need. Price from your costs and hours first, then check that the value ratio leaves members feeling they got a bargain.

How many shares do I need to break even?

Fixed season costs divided by what each share contributes after item costs, box costs, fees and your own pay. If that contribution is zero or negative, no number of shares fixes it and the price or the box has to change.

It is not financial, tax, legal or business advice, and you are responsible for verifying its output and for the numbers you enter. The worked example is illustrative arithmetic, not a forecast of how many members you will sign.

CSA SHARE PRICING CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What should a CSA share cost?

A small farm sells a season of weekly produce boxes up front. A share that looks fair to members can still pay the farmer a few dollars an hour. List what goes in the box and the weeks it runs, and see what a member gets at retail, what the season pays you per hour, the price that pays your target wage, the number of shares you need to break even, and how the answer moves if sign-ups react to price.

For market gardens, small vegetable farms and farmer-led CSAs. Nothing is uploaded: the text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device.

    Prefer a CLI?

    Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

    node cli.mjs price box.csv --weeks 20 --shares 60 --price 500
cat box.csv | node cli.mjs price - --json

    Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: How to price a CSA share: the math.

    What's recognised

    InputHandling

    The answer is exact for the numbers you type. Land, equipment depreciation, taxes, crop failure, refunds and members who leave mid-season are not modelled; put them in fixed costs if they matter to you.

    Common questions

    Does it upload my box list?

    No. The browser page works on the text you paste, in your own browser, and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.

    Why does it say my share loses money when the box looks full?

    Retail value is what a member would pay at a store; your cost is the seeds, inputs, packing, delivery and the hours you put in. Many CSAs charge a price that covers inputs but not their own labour. The tool shows the price that pays you a target hourly wage, so the gap is visible before the season starts.

    What is the price sweep based on?

    On an elasticity you choose: members are assumed to fall as the price rises by (price / base price) raised to minus the elasticity, capped at your capacity. It is an assumption, not a measurement, so read it as a way to see the trade-off between fewer members and a higher price, not a forecast.

    What does the value ratio mean?

    Retail value of a season of boxes divided by the share price. Members compare you with the store, so a ratio under 1 is a hard sell and a ratio well over 1 means there is room to raise the price.
